It starts with a short, time-boxed documentation phase (design brief, content inventory, wireframes, tokens, motion spec, architecture) because no code is written until the big decisions have written answers. A deployed, themed, budgeted skeleton then proves hosting, CI, theming and reduced-motion handling before anything is built on top. Next comes a content-complete site with navigation, resume and copy-email, so the recruiter fast path works before any motion is layered on. The motion system and the signature project rail (reference 539: hover/lift on desktop, swipe and tap on touch, focused overlay) come after that. The rail is the first real use of the animation layer, and the phase ends with measured keep-or-drop decisions on react-spring and LazyMotion. Section treatments (experience cards, skills slider, education card, hero text effect) follow. Real-device hardening and the additive cutover into `aa-phan.github.io` come last, so the v1 iPod site stays live and rollback stays trivial until the new site has passed every gate.\n6\t\n7\t## Phases\n8\t\n9\t**Phase Numbering:**\n10\t\n11\t- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work\n12\t- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)\n13\t\n14\tDecimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.\n15\t\n16\t- [x] **Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation** - Time-boxed design, content, IA, tokens, motion and architecture docs that gate all code (completed 2026-10-09)\n17\t- [x] **Phase 2: Deployed Themed Skeleton** - Vite/React/TS/Tailwind app live on the project URL with CI, JS budget, light/dark tokens and one motion-preference source (completed 2026-10-26)\n18\t- [ ] **Phase 3: Content-Complete Site** - All six sections with real content, resume download, copy-email and navigation, passing the 10-second phone test\n19\t- [ ] **Phase 4: Motion System and Signature Rail** - Shared motion rules plus the handled-object project rail with overlay, touch and keyboard paths\n20\t- [ ] **Phase 5: Section Treatments** - Expandable experience cards, skills slider, education card and hero text effect\n21\t- [ ] **Phase 6: Hardening and Cutover** - Lighthouse, real-device, keyboard/VoiceOver/axe gates, launch assets, and the additive cutover with a written rollback\n22\t\n23\t## Phase Details\n24\t\n25\t### Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation\n26\t\n27\t**Goal:** As a site owner, I want to have time-boxed design, content, motion and architecture docs, so that every major decision is settled before any code is written.\n28\t**Mode:** mvp\n29\t**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)\n30\t**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-05, DOC-06, CNT-03\n31\t**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):\n32\t\n33\t  1. It starts with a short, time-boxed documentation phase (design brief, content inventory, wireframes, tokens, motion spec, architecture) because no code is written until the big decisions have written answers. A deployed, themed, budgeted skeleton then proves hosting, CI, theming and reduced-motion handling before anything is built on top. Next comes a content-complete site with navigation, resume and copy-email, so the recruiter fast path works before any motion is layered on. The motion system and the signature project rail (reference 539: hover/lift on desktop, swipe and tap on touch, focused overlay) come after that. The rail is the first real use of the animation layer, and the phase ends with measured keep-or-drop decisions on react-spring and LazyMotion. Section treatments (experience cards, skills slider, education card, hero text effect) follow. Real-device hardening and the additive cutover into `aa-phan.github.io` come last, so the v1 iPod site stays live and rollback stays trivial until the new site has passed every gate.\n\n## Phases\n\n**Phase Numbering:**\n\n- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work\n- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)\n\nDecimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.\n\n- [x] **Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation** - Time-boxed design, content, IA, tokens, motion and architecture docs that gate all code (completed 2026-10-09)\n- [x] **Phase 2: Deployed Themed Skeleton** - Vite/React/TS/Tailwind app live on the project URL with CI, JS budget, light/dark tokens and one motion-preference source (completed 2026-10-26)\n- [ ] **Phase 3: Content-Complete Site** - All six sections with real content, resume download, copy-email and navigation, passing the 10-second phone test\n- [ ] **Phase 4: Motion System and Signature Rail** - Shared motion rules plus the handled-object project rail with overlay, touch and keyboard paths\n- [ ] **Phase 5: Section Treatments** - Expandable experience cards, skills slider, education card and hero text effect\n- [ ] **Phase 6: Hardening and Cutover** - Lighthouse, real-device, keyboard/VoiceOver/axe gates, launch assets, and the additive cutover with a written rollback\n\n## Phase Details\n\n### Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation\n\n**Goal:** As a site owner, I want to have time-boxed design, content, motion and architecture docs, so that every major decision is settled before any code is written.\n**Mode:** mvp\n**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)\n**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-05, DOC-06, CNT-03\n**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):\n\n  1. composition-only structure, typed content modules, and CSS-variable theming. No router, no global store, no data fetching.\n58\t\n59\t**Key Characteristics:**\n60\t- One page, one route. `src/app/Page.tsx` renders all sections in a single `<main id=\"main\">`. The 404 page is a separate static entry (`404.html`).\n61\t- Props flow down from `Page.tsx`. Three contexts only: theme, motion preference, toast (plus optional active-section state in `useActiveSection`).\n62\t- Content is data. Order and featured status come from `src/content/*.ts` arrays and fields, not from component logic.\n63\t- Enforced import boundaries via oxlint `no-restricted-imports` per-folder overrides in `.oxlintrc.json`, described in `docs/architecture.md`.\n64\t- Build-time gates (`scripts/check-*.mjs`) enforce budget, phone-number absence, colors, contrast, image formats.\n65\t\n66\t## Layers\n67\t\n68\t**App (composition root):**\n69\t- Purpose: Bootstrap, providers, and the only content-to-section wiring\n70\t- Location: `src/main.tsx`, `src/app/`\n71\t- Contains: `App.tsx`, `Providers.tsx`, `Page.tsx`\n72\t- Depends on: `src/anim` (via Providers), `src/components/ui/Toast`, `src/content`, `src/sections`, `src/layout`, `src/hooks`\n73\t- Used by: Vite entry (`index.html`)\n74\t\n75\t**Sections:**\n76\t- Purpose: Render each portfolio section from props\n77\t- Location: `src/sections/` (Hero, About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education, Contact)\n78\t- Contains: `*.tsx` components; Browser loads `index.html`, which includes an inline theme-init script that sets `data-theme` before first paint (`index.html`, `src/lib/theme.ts`)\n124\t2. Module script `src/main.tsx` loads the Archivo font CSS and styles, then creates the root (`src/main.tsx`)\n125\t3. `App` wraps `Page` in `Providers` (`src/app/App.tsx`, `src/app/Providers.tsx`)\n126\t4. `Providers` sets up `MotionPreferenceProvider`, then lazy `MotionFeatures`, then `ToastProvider` (`src/app/Providers.tsx`)\n127\t5. `Page` reads `siteContent` from `src/content/index.ts`, derives the email from the `email` contact, and splits other contacts (`src/app/Page.tsx`)\n128\t6. `Page` renders sections with props; `useActiveSection(SECTION_IDS)` feeds `SiteHeader` and `PillNav` (`src/app/Page.tsx`, `src/layout/nav-items.ts`)\n129\t\n130\t### Theme toggle\n131\t\n132\t1. User activates `ThemeToggle` (`src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx`), which uses `ThemeThumb` physics wrapper (`src/anim/physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`)\n133\t2. `useTheme` (`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`) updates the `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` and writes the choice to `localStorage` through `src/lib/theme.ts`\n134\t3. CSS variables in `src/styles/tokens.css` update all surfaces; no re-mount\n135\t\n136\t### Scroll-spy and navigation\n137\t\n138\t1. `useActiveSection` observes section ids with IntersectionObserver (`src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`)\n139\t2. `activeId` updates `SiteHeader` (`src/layout/SiteHeader.tsx`) and `PillNav` (`src/layout/PillNav.tsx`)\n140\t3. Navigation click calls `lockTo` to hold the active id during smooth scroll\n141\t\n142\t### Project detail\n143\t\n144\t1. Click or tap on a project in `src/sections/Projects/Projects.tsx` sets local state\n145\t2. `ProjectDialog.tsx` opens with focus handling; dialog accessibility is recorded in `docs/adr/0006-project-overlay-dialog-accessibility.md` and `docs/adr/0009-native-dialog-for-project-details.md`\n146\t\n147\t**State Management:**\n148\t- Local component state and props. Theme, motion preference and toast each have a context. No global store.\n149\t\n150\t## Key Abstractions\n151\t\n152\t**Content schema:**\n153\t- Purpose: Typed shape for all copy and data\n154\t- Examples: `src/content/schema.ts` (`Profile`, `Project`, `ExperienceEntry`, `EducationEntry`, `SkillGroup`, `ContactLink`, `DateRange`, `ImageAsset`, `Writeup`)\n155\t- Pattern: Content modules use `satisfies` against the schema so missing fields fail `tsc -b`\n156\t\n157\t**Animation facade:**\n158\t- Purpose: Hide library choice from sections and layout\n159\t- Examples: `src/anim/index.ts` exports `ThemeThumb`, `MotionPreferenceProvider`, `useMotionPreference`, `springs`, `durations`, `easeOut`, `MotionFeatures`, `ToastPresence`, `NavIndicator`, `PillMorph`\n160\t- Pattern: One library animates any given element. Each wrapper reads the motion preference and renders an instant equivalent when reduced.\n161\t\n162\t**Design tokens:**\n163\t- Purpose: Five role colors per theme drive all surfaces\n164\t- Examples: `src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/styles/index.css` (`@custom-variant` dark bound to `[data-theme=dark]`, `@theme inline` mapping)\n165\t- Pattern: Derived tokens computed with `color-mix(in oklch, ...)`\n166\t\n167\t**Vendored primitive:**\n168\t- Purpose: Ready-made text effect kept in the repo\n169\t- Examples: `src/components/motion-primitives/text-effect.tsx`\n170\t- Pattern: Treated as owned source; excluded from lint autofix churn\n171\t\n172\t## Entry Points\n173\t\n174\t**Browser entry (SPA):**\n175\t- Location: `index.html` loads `src/main.tsx`\n176\t- Triggers: Page load of `/` (or `${BASE_URL}`)\n177\t- Responsibilities: Mount React, apply global CSS and font\n178\t\n179\t**404 entry:**\n180\t- Location: `404.html` (second Vite input in `vite.config.ts`)\n181\t- Triggers: GitHub Pages serving unknown paths\n182\t- Responsibilities: Static not-found page styled by `src/styles/not-found.css`\n183\t\n184\t**Build entry:**\n185\t- Location: `vite.config.ts`\n186\t- Triggers: `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, `npm run preview`\n187\t- Responsibilities: base path from `VITE_BASE`, plugins, `@` alias, multi-page inputs\n188\t\n189\t**CI entries:**\n190\t- Location: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`\n191\t- Triggers: push and pull_request (CI); push to `main` and manual dispatch (deploy)\n192\t- Responsibilities: `npm run verify`, Playwright e2e, Pages deployment\n193\t\n194\t## Architectural Constraints\n195\t\n196\t- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser main thread. No workers. No server.\n197\t- **Global state:** No global store. Overview\n\n```text\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                 Entry: `index.html` -> `src/main.tsx`                 │\n│ Bootstrap | Mounts React root in StrictMode, imports font and global CSS | `src/main.tsx` |\n| App shell | Wraps the page in providers | `src/app/App.tsx` |\n| Providers | Motion preference, lazy motion features, toast context | `src/app/Providers.tsx` |\n| Page | Assembles sections; sole consumer of `siteContent`; runs scroll-spy | `src/app/Page.tsx` |\n| Content model | Type definitions and typed data modules | `src/content/schema.ts`, `src/content/index.ts` |\n| Section components | Props in, JSX out, one folder per section | `src/sections/*/` |\n| Layout | Header, pill nav, footer, skip link, container | `src/layout/` |\n| UI primitives | CTA link, theme toggle, toast, inline SVG icons | `src/components/ui/` |\n| Animation facade | Single public import path for animation | `src/anim/index.ts` |\n| Theme logic | Storage, `data-theme` attribute, theme hook | `src/lib/theme.ts`, `src/hooks/useTheme.ts` |\n| Scroll-spy | IntersectionObserver over section ids | `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts` |\n| Styles | Tailwind entry, tokens, base resets, reduced-motion guard | `src/styles/index.css`, `src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/styles/base.css` |\n\n## Pattern Overview\n\n**Overall:** Static single-page React app with composition-only structure, typed content modules, and CSS-variable theming. No router, no global store, no data fetching.\n\n**Key Characteristics:**\n- One page, one route. `src/app/Page.tsx` renders all sections in a single `<main id=\"main\">`. The 404 page is a separate static entry (`404.html`).\n- Props flow down from `Page.tsx`. Three contexts only: theme, motion preference, toast (plus optional active-section state in `useActiveSection`).\n- Content is data. Order and featured status come from `src/content/*.ts` arrays and fields, not from component logic.\n- Enforced import boundaries via oxlint `no-restricted-imports` per-folder overrides in `.oxlintrc.json`, described in `docs/architecture.md`.\n- Build-time gates (`scripts/check-*.mjs`) enforce budget, phone-number absence, colors, contrast, image formats.\n\n## Layers\n\n**App (composition root):**\n- Purpose: Bootstrap, providers, and the only content-to-section wiring\n- Location: `src/main.tsx`, `src/app/`\n- Contains: `App.tsx`, `Providers.tsx`, `Page.tsx`\n- Depends on: `src/anim` (via Providers), `src/components/ui/Toast`, `src/content`, `src/sections`, `src/layout`, `src/hooks`\n- Used by: Vite entry (`index.html`)\n\n**Sections:**\n- Purpose: Render each portfolio section from props\n- Location: `src/sections/` (Hero, About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education, Contact)\n- Contains: `*.tsx` components; Projects also has `ProjectDialog.tsx`, `Sleeve.tsx`, `project-types.ts`\n- Depends on: `src/layout`, `src/components/ui`, `src/anim` barrel, `src/content` types, `src/lib`\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`\n\n**Layout:**\n- Purpose: Site chrome and structural primitives\n- Location: `src/layout/`\n- Contains: `SiteHeader.tsx`, `PillNav.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`, `SkipLink.tsx`, `Container.tsx`, `Section.tsx`, `Wordmark.tsx`, `nav-items.ts`\n- Depends on: `src/anim` barrel, `src/hooks`, `src/lib`, `src/components/ui`\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`, sections\n\n**Components / UI:**\n- Purpose: Reusable widgets and icons\n- Location: `src/components/ui/`, `src/components/motion-primitives/`\n- Contains: `CtaLink.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `Toast.tsx`, `useToast.ts`, `useCopyEmail.ts`, `icons/*.tsx`, `text-effect.tsx` (vendored, unrendered in the hero role line)\n- Depends on: `src/anim` barrel, `src/lib`\n- Used by: layout, sections\n\n**Animation:**\n- Purpose: Only place that touches motion libraries; provides semantic wrappers\n- Location: `src/anim/`\n- Contains: `index.ts` barrel, `MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`, `useMotionPreference.ts`, `MotionFeatures.tsx` (LazyMotion), `tokens.ts` (springs and durations), `declarative/` (ToastPresence, NavIndicator, PillMorph), `physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`, `features.ts`, `featuresStatus.ts`\n- Depends on: `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`, `src/components/motion-primitives`\n- Used by: layout, sections, components, app providers\n\n**Hooks and lib:**\n- Purpose: Shared behavior and utilities\n- Location: `src/hooks/` (`useActiveSection.ts`, `useTheme.ts`), `src/lib/` (`theme.ts`, `utils.ts` with `cn`, `dates.ts`, `copy.ts`)\n- Used by: almost every layer\n\n**Styles and assets:**\n- Purpose: Design tokens, theming, global CSS, images\n- Location: `src/styles/`, `src/assets/images/`, `public/`\n- Used by: all components via Tailwind utilities that map to CSS variables\n\n**Content:**\n- Purpose: All copy and data\n- Location: `src/content/` (`profile.ts`, `experience.ts`, `projects.ts`, `skills.ts`, `education.ts`, `contacts.ts`, `images.ts`, `schema.ts`, `index.ts`)\n- Depends on: `src/assets/images` for image imports, `src/content/schema.ts` types\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx` only\n\n## Data Flow\n\n### Primary Request Path (page load)\n\n1. Browser loads `index.html`, which includes an inline theme-init script that sets `data-theme` before first paint (`index.html`, `src/lib/theme.ts`)\n2. Module script `src/main.tsx` loads the Archivo font CSS and styles, then creates the root (`src/main.tsx`)\n3. `App` wraps `Page` in `Providers` (`src/app/App.tsx`, `src/app/Providers.tsx`)\n4. `Providers` sets up `MotionPreferenceProvider`, then lazy `MotionFeatures`, then `ToastProvider` (`src/app/Providers.tsx`)\n5. `Page` reads `siteContent` from `src/content/index.ts`, derives the email from the `email` contact, and splits other contacts (`src/app/Page.tsx`)\n6. `Page` renders sections with props; `useActiveSection(SECTION_IDS)` feeds `SiteHeader` and `PillNav` (`src/app/Page.tsx`, `src/layout/nav-items.ts`)\n\n### Theme toggle\n\n1. User activates `ThemeToggle` (`src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx`), which uses `ThemeThumb` physics wrapper (`src/anim/physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`)\n2. `useTheme` (`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`) updates the `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` and writes the choice to `localStorage` through `src/lib/theme.ts`\n3. CSS variables in `src/styles/tokens.css` update all surfaces; no re-mount\n\n### Scroll-spy and navigation\n\n1. `useActiveSection` observes section ids with IntersectionObserver (`src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`)\n2. `activeId` updates `SiteHeader` (`src/layout/SiteHeader.tsx`) and `PillNav` (`src/layout/PillNav.tsx`)\n3. Navigation click calls `lockTo` to hold the active id during smooth scroll\n\n### Project detail\n\n1. Click or tap on a project in `src/sections/Projects/Projects.tsx` sets local state\n2. `ProjectDialog.tsx` opens with focus handling; dialog accessibility is recorded in `docs/adr/0006-project-overlay-dialog-accessibility.md` and `docs/adr/0009-native-dialog-for-project-details.md`\n\n**State Management:**\n- Local component state and props. Theme, motion preference and toast each have a context. No global store.\n\n## Key Abstractions\n\n**Content schema:**\n- Purpose: Typed shape for all copy and data\n- Examples: `src/content/schema.ts` (`Profile`, `Project`, `ExperienceEntry`, `EducationEntry`, `SkillGroup`, `ContactLink`, `DateRange`, `ImageAsset`, `Writeup`)\n- Pattern: Content modules use `satisfies` against the schema so missing fields fail `tsc -b`\n\n**Animation facade:**\n- Purpose: Hide library choice from sections and layout\n- Examples: `src/anim/index.ts` exports `ThemeThumb`, `MotionPreferenceProvider`, `useMotionPreference`, `springs`, `durations`, `easeOut`, `MotionFeatures`, `ToastPresence`, `NavIndicator`, `PillMorph`\n- Pattern: One library animates any given element. Each wrapper reads the motion preference and renders an instant equivalent when reduced.\n\n**Design tokens:**\n- Purpose: Five role colors per theme drive all surfaces\n- Examples: `src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/styles/index.css` (`@custom-variant` dark bound to `[data-theme=dark]`, `@theme inline` mapping)\n- Pattern: Derived tokens computed with `color-mix(in oklch, ...)`\n\n**Vendored primitive:**\n- Purpose: Ready-made text effect kept in the repo\n- Examples: `src/components/motion-primitives/text-effect.tsx`\n- Pattern: Treated as owned source; excluded from lint autofix churn\n\n## Entry Points\n\n**Browser entry (SPA):**\n- Location: `index.html` loads `src/main.tsx`\n- Triggers: Page load of `/` (or `${BASE_URL}`)\n- Responsibilities: Mount React, apply global CSS and font\n\n**404 entry:**\n- Location: `404.html` (second Vite input in `vite.config.ts`)\n- Triggers: GitHub Pages serving unknown paths\n- Responsibilities: Static not-found page styled by `src/styles/not-found.css`\n\n**Build entry:**\n- Location: `vite.config.ts`\n- Triggers: `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, `npm run preview`\n- Responsibilities: base path from `VITE_BASE`, plugins, `@` alias, multi-page inputs\n\n**CI entries:**\n- Location: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`\n- Triggers: push and pull_request (CI); push to `main` and manual dispatch (deploy)\n- Responsibilities: `npm run verify`, Playwright e2e, Pages deployment\n\n## Architectural Constraints\n\n- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser main thread. No workers. No server.\n- **Global state:** No global store. Module-level config in `src/anim/tokens.ts` (springs and durations, read-only exports). `localStorage` key for the theme is the only persistent state.\n- **Circular imports:** None documented. Import direction is enforced downward by lint rules.\n- **Single content consumer:** Only `src/app/Page.tsx` may import content data. Sections receive data as props.\n- **Animation isolation:** Only `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/` may import `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web`.\n- **Build output:** Static `dist/` only. Initial JS budget enforced at 150 kB gzipped by `scripts/check-js-budget.mjs`.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Importing content data outside Page\n\n**What happens:** A section or layout component imports from `src/content/*` directly.\n**Why it's wrong:** Breaks the layer rule in `docs/architecture.md` and the oxlint boundary in `.oxlintrc.json`. Makes ordering and copy changes non-local.\n**Do this instead:** Add the field to the schema in `src/content/schema.ts`, populate it in the content module, and pass it down as a prop from `src/app/Page.tsx`.\n\n### Importing motion libraries outside the animation layer\n\n**What happens:** A section or layout component imports `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n**Why it's wrong:** The rule \"one library animates any given element\" and the reduced-motion contract depend on the wrapper. Lint fails CI.\n**Do this instead:** Use the wrapper exported from `src/anim/index.ts`. Add a new wrapper under `src/anim/declarative/` or `src/anim/physics/` if none fits.\n\n### Raw color values in components\n\n**What happens:** Hex, rgb, hsl, oklch or Tailwind default palette utilities in components.\n**Why it's wrong:** The check `scripts/check-colors.mjs` fails the build, and palette swaps stop being a one-block edit.\n**Do this instead:** Use semantic utilities mapped in `src/styles/index.css` and values from `src/styles/tokens.css`.\n\n## Error Handling\n\n**Strategy:** Static content with compile-time checks. No runtime error boundaries or network error paths were found.\n\n**Patterns:**\n- Typecheck of content via `satisfies` against `src/content/schema.ts`\n- Content tests in `tests/unit/content.test.ts` check unique ids, resolved related ids, alt text, https external links and date order\n- Build-time gates in `scripts/` fail `npm run verify`\n\n## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n\n**Logging:** None at runtime.\n**Validation:** Compile-time via TypeScript and content tests. Build gates for phone number, images and colors.\n**Authentication:** Not applicable.\n\n---\n\n*Architecture analysis: 2026-11-20*\n","numLines":241,"startLine":1,"totalLines":241}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01AXdowv2wXBXMf6jXvtz5RC","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

<action>\n123\tAll four files live in the phase directory per D-01; wireframes are ASCII/markdown per D-02. This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n124\t\n125\t(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n126\t- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n127\t- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n128\t- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n129\t\n130\t(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n\n(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n\n(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". One format is used for every date on the site and in this file.\n\n1. Month names are written in full: January, February, and so on. No abbreviations, no numeric months.\n2. A single date is `Month YYYY`, for example `July 2026`.\n3. A range is `Month YYYY – Month YYYY`: an en dash (U+2013) with one space on each side, and the year written on both sides, for example `May 2025 – August 2025`.\n4. Resume abbreviations are expanded. The resume's `Aug. 2022` becomes `August 2022`.\n5. Legacy hyphen ranges and short months are normalized. The legacy `June 2023 - Aug 2023` becomes `June 2023 – August 2023`.\n6. Academic-term labels (Spring 2024, Fall 2023, Summer 2022) are converted to month ranges per the G-08 ruling. The original label is kept in the item's Legacy-site value.\n7. This policy is applied to every date in the file. WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n10\t\n11\t## Format\n12\t\n13\tTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n14\t\n15\t- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n16\t- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n17\t- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n18\t\n19\tA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n20\t\n21\tVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n22\t\n23\tRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n24\t\n25\t## Role tokens\n26\t\n27\tThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. It carries no contrast requirement and is never the only cue for a control boundary; controls use `--border-strong` (3:1).\n356\t- Disabled controls are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, but they still get a non-color cue (reduced weight plus a \"not available\" affordance such as a dashed outline), not color alone.\n357\t- `--secondary` is a fill. It is never used as text or as a lone border.\n358\t\n359\t## Chosen system\n360\t\n361\tCandidate D, neutral grounds with the tuned seed indigo as signal (Phase 3, D-02; the Phase 1 pick was candidate A, which stays recorded above). 03-03, decisions D-03 and D-06): Archivo Variable replaces Inter, and the 1.2 modular scale is replaced by the poster ladder. This section describes what ships.\n430\t\n431\tPairing: one family. Archivo Variable for display and body: `@fontsource-variable/archivo` 5.3.0 (CSS family name `'Archivo Variable'`), no JS. Archivo ships a width axis, so the same family covers the compressed day headings and the widened night wordmark. There is no second face (DSN-04 allows at most 2 declared families; the page declares Archivo Variable plus its local metric fallback `'Archivo Fallback'`, which is a rule over a system font, not a download).\n432\t\n433\t- Import: `@fontsource-variable/archivo/wdth.css` in `main.tsx` (declares `font-display: swap`, weight 100 to 900, `font-stretch` 62% to 125%, per-script `unicode-range`). The latin woff2 is 90,104 B, about 42 kB more than Inter's 48 kB latin file; latin-ext and vietnamese are only fetched if the copy uses those scripts.\n434\t- Fallback stacks: `--font-sans` and `--font-display`: `'Archivo Variable', 'Archivo Fallback', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif`. Monospace for code or the email address if needed: `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace` (system, no package).\n435\t- Metric fallback: `'Archivo Fallback'` is declared in `base.css` as two `@font-face` rules over local Arial (weights 100 to 599, `size-adjust` 100.9%) and local Arial Bold (weights 600 to 900, `size-adjust` 103.1%), with ascent and descent overrides of Archivo's 0.90 and 0.25 em divided by `size-adjust` and a zero line gap. Plan 01-04 added candidates B and C, the full 19-pair list for every section, the type pairing per candidate, and, after the user picked candidate A (tuned seed indigo, Inter only), the chosen system below.\n\nOwner decisions this file records: D-04 (three candidates, per-theme tokens, the user picks one), D-05 (type explored with color), D-06 (exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints). WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n\n## Format\n\nTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n\n- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n\nA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n\nVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n\nRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n\n## Role tokens\n\nThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. Per-theme values are mandatory (D-04): the seed indigo `2f27ce` measures 2.23:1 on the dark background `050315`, which fails text, UI and focus use.\n\n| Order | Token | Job |\n|-------|-------|-----|\n| 1 | `--text` | Body and heading text, and the on-color for filled dark surfaces |\n| 2 | `--background` | Page background |\n| 3 | `--primary` | Filled buttons, the main brand fill |\n| 4 | `--secondary` | Tint family for cards and soft fills (decorative, never text or a border on its own: `dedcff` on the light background is 1.29:1) |\n| 5 | `--accent` | Highlights and large display color |\n\nDerived tokens (D-06), all `mix()` of roles, defined once for every candidate in the shared `derived` block:\n\n| Token | Job |\n|-------|-----|\n| `--surface` | Card, toast and overlay panel fill |\n| `--muted` | Dates, captions and secondary copy |\n| `--border` | Decorative hairlines (no contrast requirement) |\n| `--border-strong` | Control boundaries (3:1) |\n| `--link` | Inline link text |\n| `--on-primary` | Label on a filled primary button |\n| `--on-accent` | Label on an accent chip or active pill |\n| `--primary-hover` | Hovered or pressed filled button |\n| `--focus-ring` | Keyboard focus indicator |\n\n## Candidate A — Tuned seed indigo\n\nChosen in Phase 1; superseded by candidate D in Phase 3 (D-02). Kept here as the recorded fallback.\n\nContinuity with the realtimecolors seed (050315 / fbfbfe / 2f27ce / dedcff / 433bff). Dark roles are authored for dark, not inverted: the text and background swap ends, primary and accent lift to the 5.66:1 and 8.19:1 class on `050315`, and secondary becomes a dark indigo tint. One tune from the seed in light: `--primary` moves from `2f27ce` to `5046e5` (plan 01-01 had first tuned it to `281fb4`; the full 19-pair set forces a second move). Reason: a focus ring must hold 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary button. With `281fb4` no ring color does all four: a mid-tone ring clears the button but gives 2.50:1 on the secondary tint, and a near-black ring gives 1.89:1 on the button. A primary lighter than the seed's (relative luminance about 0.11 to 0.18) opens the band: a near-black ring then reads on the button (3.2:1 or better) and on every light surface, while the white label on the button still holds 4.5:1. it is the home link), the six section links (Experience, Projects, About, Skills, Education, Contact), the theme toggle [IX-10] and a Resume button, with a scroll-spy indicator under the active link [IX-08]. The bottom pill is not shown at this width.\n38\t- Below 768 px a non-fixed top bar sits above the hero (D-19): the wordmark on the left and the theme toggle on the right, visible on first paint. A thumb-reachable bottom pill nav is fixed to the viewport. Collapsed, it has three segments: Experience, Projects and Menu. Experience and Projects jump straight to their section; the Menu segment morphs the pill in place into a panel of the six section links, the theme toggle and Resume [IX-07] (reference 445). The panel carries Contact Me.\n39\t- A skip link is the first focusable element and targets {#main}.\n40\t- Nav form is chosen by width. Hover effects are chosen by pointer capability, never by width.\n41\t- Nav links are plain anchors in a single page: there is no router, and the URL changes only by the browser's own hash handling.\n42\t\n43\t## Recruiter fast path (10-second test)\n44\t\n45\tA first-time visitor on a 375 px phone reaches each item with at most one tap from the first viewport.\n46\t\n47\t| Item       | Where at 375                                                    | Taps from first viewport |\n48\t| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |\n49\t| Name       | The h1 in the hero, visible on first paint                      | 0                        |\n50\t| Role       | The role line directly under the name                           | 0                        |\n51\t| Experience | The Experience segment of the collapsed pill nav                | 1                        |\n52\t| Projects   | The Projects segment of the collapsed pill nav                  | 1                        |\n53\t| Resume     | The Download resume CTA in the hero                             | 1                        |\n54\t| Contact    | The Copy email CTA in the hero (Contact Me is in the pill menu) | 1                        |\n55\t\n56\tPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled (the same rule as the design brief).\n57\t\n58\t## Above the fold @ 375\n59\t\n60\tA 375 x 667 viewport shows, top to bottom:\n61\t\n62\t- The top bar with the wordmark and the theme toggle.\n63\t- The name as the h1, \"Aaron\" over \"Phan\".\n64\t- The role line under it, plain text from first paint (the text effect [IX-01] arrives in Phase 5).\n65\t- The Download resume and Copy email CTAs, each at least 44 px tall. Every other section has one h2, and each section element is labelled by its heading with `aria-labelledby`.\n76\t- Section anchors are the seven in the registry above; nav links and CTAs are plain `<a href=\"#anchor\">`.\n77\t- Each section carries `scroll-margin-top` equal to the sticky nav height at 768 px and up, and the height of the safe top area at 375, so a link jump never hides a heading.\n78\t\n79\t## Project rail and overlay behavior\n80\t\n81\tFeatured order: PRJ-01, PRJ-02, PRJ-03, then PRJ-04, PRJ-05, PRJ-06, PRJ-07 (the remaining projects, newest first).\n82\t\n83\t- The rail is native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap on touch [IX-04] and a hover lift with neighbor shift on a fine pointer [IX-03], with the same lift on keyboard focus [IX-06].\n84\t- Opening a project shows an overlay with the index written as NN / 07. Prev and next wrap around (07 / 07 goes to 01 / 07). The overlay has a Close button; Escape closes it; focus returns to the rail item that opened it; the URL does not change (deep-linkable project URLs are a deferred requirement).\n85\t- Dialog accessibility is settled by ADR-0006: focus trap, inert background, scroll lock and focus return belong to the dialog primitive, and motion animates only the morph [IX-05].\n86\t- Project links and images are deferred (G-01, G-02), so overlay links show only when supplied and rail cards use a cover placeholder.\n87\t\n88\t## Global behaviors\n89\t\n90\t- Press-squish [IX-02] on all buttons and cards, on the inner surface only.\n91\t- Section reveals [IX-15] when a section enters the viewport; content is visible by default and the hidden start state is set after mount.\n92\t- Desktop smooth wheel scroll [IX-16], off on touch and under reduced motion.\n93\t- Desktop pointer polish [IX-17]: Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on the hero and contact CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards, fine pointer only.\n94\t\n95\t## Frame conventions\n96\t\n97\t- Frames are drawn in a fenced `text` block with printable ASCII only. The width counts the whole line including both `|` borders: 38 characters for 375 px, 64 for 768 px and 96 for 1280 px (so the inner width is 36, 62 and 94).\n98\t- Square-bracket annotations name an interaction ID from `01-MOTION-SPEC.md` (for example [IX-09]) or an anchor (for example [#contact]).\n99\t- `[ Label ]` is a button. `Label >` is a link. `(( ))` marks the toast. `=====` borders the bottom pill nav and its expanded panel on mobile. `#` borders mark a visible focus ring. `:::` marks a blurred backdrop. `( )` around a word is a chip, `[logo]` and `[ O ]` are logo and monogram chips.\n100\t- Touch targets are at least 44 px high and wide at 375 px.\n101\t- The fixed bottom pill is drawn only where it matters (Hero, Contact, the nav states); the sticky top nav is drawn in the Hero frames and the nav state frames. Dates in frames use an ASCII hyphen; on the site they are written with an en dash per the date policy in the inventory.\n102\t- Copy in frames is abbreviated where it does not fit (for example short month names at 375). Plan 01-07 set the final section order and added the hero, nav, rail, overlay and every other section at 375, 768 and 1280 px.\n\nWireframes are ASCII inside this markdown file (D-02). No HTML sketches.\n\n## Section registry\n\nSeven fixed anchors. Every phase doc refers to a section by its anchor, never by a position number. The page order is in the next section.\n\n| Anchor        | Section    |\n| ------------- | ---------- |\n| {#hero}       | Hero       |\n| {#experience} | Experience |\n| {#projects}   | Projects   |\n| {#about}      | About Me   |\n| {#skills}     | Skills     |\n| {#education}  | Education  |\n| {#contact}    | Contact Me |\n\n## Section order\n\n| Order | Section    | Anchor        | Why here                                                                                                       |\n| ----- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| 1     | Hero       | {#hero}       | Name, role and the Resume and Copy email CTAs are visible at first paint, which is most of the 10-second test. |\n| 2     | Experience | {#experience} | Recruiters look for experience first; it is the first thing below the fold and one pill tap from anywhere.     |\n| 3     | Projects   | {#projects}   | The signature rail and overlay; it follows Experience so the work sits next to the roles it came from.         |\n| 4     | About Me   | {#about}      | Personality (the DJ side) comes after the evidence, and links to the Instagram in Contact.                     |\n| 5     | Skills     | {#skills}     | A scan-friendly summary once the reader knows the work.                                                        |\n| 6     | Education  | {#education}  | Short, factual, needed for the GPA and degree check, but rarely the first stop.                                |\n| 7     | Contact Me | {#contact}    | The page ends on the action; it is also one tap from the hero CTA and the pill nav.                            |\n\n## Navigation model\n\n- 768 px and wider use a sticky top nav, always visible, on a solid ground (D-18): the wordmark top left (PHAN in the light theme, PHVNTM in the dark theme; it is the home link), the six section links (Experience, Projects, About, Skills, Education, Contact), the theme toggle [IX-10] and a Resume button, with a scroll-spy indicator under the active link [IX-08]. The bottom pill is not shown at this width.\n- Below 768 px a non-fixed top bar sits above the hero (D-19): the wordmark on the left and the theme toggle on the right, visible on first paint. A thumb-reachable bottom pill nav is fixed to the viewport. Collapsed, it has three segments: Experience, Projects and Menu. Experience and Projects jump straight to their section; the Menu segment morphs the pill in place into a panel of the six section links, the theme toggle and Resume [IX-07] (reference 445). The panel carries Contact Me.\n- A skip link is the first focusable element and targets {#main}.\n- Nav form is chosen by width. Hover effects are chosen by pointer capability, never by width.\n- Nav links are plain anchors in a single page: there is no router, and the URL changes only by the browser's own hash handling.\n\n## Recruiter fast path (10-second test)\n\nA first-time visitor on a 375 px phone reaches each item with at most one tap from the first viewport.\n\n| Item       | Where at 375                                                    | Taps from first viewport |\n| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |\n| Name       | The h1 in the hero, visible on first paint                      | 0                        |\n| Role       | The role line directly under the name                           | 0                        |\n| Experience | The Experience segment of the collapsed pill nav                | 1                        |\n| Projects   | The Projects segment of the collapsed pill nav                  | 1                        |\n| Resume     | The Download resume CTA in the hero                             | 1                        |\n| Contact    | The Copy email CTA in the hero (Contact Me is in the pill menu) | 1                        |\n\nPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled (the same rule as the design brief).\n\n## Above the fold @ 375\n\nA 375 x 667 viewport shows, top to bottom:\n\n- The top bar with the wordmark and the theme toggle.\n- The name as the h1, \"Aaron\" over \"Phan\".\n- The role line under it, plain text from first paint (the text effect [IX-01] arrives in Phase 5).\n- The Download resume and Copy email CTAs, each at least 44 px tall. There is no Contact link in the hero.\n- The two corner facts under the CTAs: \"Graduating December 2026, UT Austin ECE\" and \"Last role: Capital One, summer 2026\".\n- The collapsed pill nav fixed at the bottom, clear of the CTAs.\n- The top edge of {#experience}, so the reader knows there is more below.\n\nThe frame is `### Frame: Hero @ 375`. Nothing in the first viewport depends on JavaScript or motion.\n\n## Anchors and landmarks\n\n- Landmarks: header (skip link and nav), nav, main {#main}, footer.\n- One h1 per page: the name in the hero. Every other section has one h2, and each section element is labelled by its heading with `aria-labelledby`.\n- Section anchors are the seven in the registry above; nav links and CTAs are plain `<a href=\"#anchor\">`.\n- Each section carries `scroll-margin-top` equal to the sticky nav height at 768 px and up, and the height of the safe top area at 375, so a link jump never hides a heading.\n\n## Project rail and overlay behavior\n\nFeatured order: PRJ-01, PRJ-02, PRJ-03, then PRJ-04, PRJ-05, PRJ-06, PRJ-07 (the remaining projects, newest first).\n\n- The rail is native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap on touch [IX-04] and a hover lift with neighbor shift on a fine pointer [IX-03], with the same lift on keyboard focus [IX-06].\n- Opening a project shows an overlay with the index written as NN / 07. Prev and next wrap around (07 / 07 goes to 01 / 07). The overlay has a Close button; Escape closes it; focus returns to the rail item that opened it; the URL does not change (deep-linkable project URLs are a deferred requirement).\n- Dialog accessibility is settled by ADR-0006: focus trap, inert background, scroll lock and focus return belong to the dialog primitive, and motion animates only the morph [IX-05].\n- Project links and images are deferred (G-01, G-02), so overlay links show only when supplied and rail cards use a cover placeholder.\n\n## Global behaviors\n\n- Press-squish [IX-02] on all buttons and cards, on the inner surface only.\n- Section reveals [IX-15] when a section enters the viewport; content is visible by default and the hidden start state is set after mount.\n- Desktop smooth wheel scroll [IX-16], off on touch and under reduced motion.\n- Desktop pointer polish [IX-17]: Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on the hero and contact CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards, fine pointer only.\n\n## Frame conventions\n\n- Frames are drawn in a fenced `text` block with printable ASCII only. The width counts the whole line including both `|` borders: 38 characters for 375 px, 64 for 768 px and 96 for 1280 px (so the inner width is 36, 62 and 94).\n- Square-bracket annotations name an interaction ID from `01-MOTION-SPEC.md` (for example [IX-09]) or an anchor (for example [#contact]).\n- `[ Label ]` is a button. `Label >` is a link. `(( ))` marks the toast. `=====` borders the bottom pill nav and its expanded panel on mobile. `#` borders mark a visible focus ring. `:::` marks a blurred backdrop. `( )` around a word is a chip, `[logo]` and `[ O ]` are logo and monogram chips.\n- Touch targets are at least 44 px high and wide at 375 px.\n- The fixed bottom pill is drawn only where it matters (Hero, Contact, the nav states); the sticky top nav is drawn in the Hero frames and the nav state frames. Dates in frames use an ASCII hyphen; on the site they are written with an en dash per the date policy in the inventory.\n- Copy in frames is abbreviated where it does not fit (for example short month names at 375). {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0196HnPaCzEyGrwL2SsuxEWK","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Motion Spec (DOC-05)\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tPhase 1 plan 01-01 seeded this file with the ownership rule, the fixed 17-row interaction catalog and the first fully specified interaction (IX-09). Plan 01-05 completed it: principles, tokens, reduced-motion layers, ownership matrix, vendored primitives, the other 16 interaction specs and the element ownership check.\n6\t\n7\t## Ownership rule\n8\t\n9\t- Exactly one library animates any element: motion, react-spring, CSS or Lenis. Never two on the same element or property.\n10\t- No Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates.\n11\t- react-spring is scoped to IX-02, IX-03, IX-06 and IX-10 (velocity-carrying, tactile physics). Everything else uses motion, CSS or Lenis as the catalog says.\n12\t\n13\t## Principles\n14\t\n15\t- Motion never gates content. Name, role and CTAs are visible at first paint. The hero text effect runs only on the role line and never delays it.\n16\t- Animate transform and opacity only, plus motion layout animations where an interaction needs them (IX-05, IX-07, IX-08, IX-11, IX-14).\n17\t- Fine-pointer effects are gated by the media query `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and carry no hover-only content (MOT-04). Touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing.\n18\t- `touch-action` is set only on small draggables. The project rail uses native horizontal scrolling, so vertical page scroll is never captured.\n19\t- Infinite or looping motion pauses when off-screen or when the tab is hidden.\n20\t- Motion budget: entrance animations take at most 420 ms; stagger is at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items; nothing blocks input.\n21\t\n22\t## Motion tokens\n23\t\n24\tCanonical home is `src/anim/tokens.ts`, with CSS mirrors `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`. One table drives both libraries so they feel like one system.\n25\t\n26\t| Token | Kind | motion format (stiffness, damping, mass) | react-spring format (tension, friction, mass) | Value |\n27\t|-------|------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|\n28\t| snappy | spring | 500, 32, 1 | 500, 32, 1 | presses, toggles |\n29\t| gentle | spring | 170, 26, 1 | 170, 26, 1 | rail lift, layout settling |\n30\t| bouncy | spring | 300, 14, 1 | 300, 14, 1 | playful overshoot, used sparingly |\n31\t| fast | duration | n/a | n/a | 120 ms |\n32\t| base | duration | n/a | n/a | 220 ms |\n33\t| slow | duration | n/a | n/a | 420 ms |\n34\t| ease-out | easing | n/a | n/a | cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) |\n35\t\n36\treact-spring `tension` equals motion `stiffness` and `friction` equals `damping`. The spring numbers are starting values, to be tuned on a real iPhone and a real Android phone during the signature-rail work (Phase 4).\n37\t\n38\t## Reduced motion\n39\t\n40\tOne preference source (MOT-01): `useMotionPreference` reads `prefers-reduced-motion` with a `change` listener (users toggle it live) and feeds three consumers:\n41\t\n42\t- motion: `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (from `motion/react`).\n43\t- react-spring: `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` from `@react-spring/web`, set in an effect with a dependency array and a cleanup that resets it.\n44\t- CSS: the guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which also gates smooth scroll behind `no-preference`.\n45\t\n46\tLenis is not started under reduced motion (MOT-05). Motion's `user` mode still animates opacity, so text effects and other opacity-driven wrappers branch manually on the hook's `reduced` value.\n47\t\n48\t| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |\n49\t|-------|-----------|--------|\n50\t| L0 Progressive enhancement | Content is visible by default in HTML and CSS. Reveal wrappers set the hidden initial state only after mount on the client, and `<noscript>` guarantees visibility. | JS failure, slow hydration, crawlers, screenshots |\n51\t| L1 CSS guard | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapses animation and transition durations to near zero, runs animations once and sets `scroll-behavior: auto`. | CSS transitions, keyframes, anchor scroll |\n52\t| L2 motion | `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (\"user\", or \"always\" and \"never\" from an override). Disables transform and layout animations, keeps opacity and color. | All motion components, including vendored primitives |\n53\t| L3 react-spring | `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` in the provider effect. Springs jump to their target. | All spring physics |\n54\t| L4 Wrapper branches | Wrappers branch on `reduced` to drop parallax and scroll-linked transforms, stop loops and autoplay (text loop, infinite slider), disable fling, and swap transforms for short fades or nothing. | What L2 and L3 do not cover |\n55\t| L5 Non-motion feedback | Pressed, focus and selected states read without motion, through color, outline or shape. | Reduced-motion users still get feedback |\n56\t| L6 Visible toggle | Optional \"Reduce motion\" control persisted to localStorage and fed into `useMotionPreference`. Open decision, not committed. | Users whose OS setting is off but who want calm |\n57\t\n58\t## Ownership matrix\n59\t\n60\tMOT-02. Every interaction class has exactly one owner.\n61\t\n62\t| Interaction class | Owner | Why |\n63\t|-------------------|-------|-----|\n64\t| Mount, unmount and presence | motion (`AnimatePresence`) | Mature exit handling under React 19 |\n65\t| Layout and shared-element morphs | motion (`layout`, `layoutId`) | react-spring has no equivalent |\n66\t| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion (`useScroll`, `whileInView`) | Already bundled |\n67\t| Text and number effects, motion-primitives prefabs | motion | The primitives are written against it |\n68\t| Velocity physics, press-squish, rail lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring (`useSpring`, `useSprings`) | Continuous retargeting gives the tactile signature |\n69\t| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail | CSS | Zero JS cost |\n70\t| Desktop wheel smoothing | Lenis | Wheel only, off on touch |\n71\t\n72\tConstraints:\n73\t\n74\t- Install `@react-spring/web` at `~10.1.x` only; never the umbrella `react-spring` package.\n75\t- Avoid `useTransition` in core UI; presence is motion's job, which keeps the react-spring v11 migration trivial.\n76\t- `@use-gesture/react` is not added up front.\n77\t- Import motion only from `motion/react`, never raw `framer-motion`.\n78\t- Whether react-spring stays at all is decided after the rail is measured (bundle cost and feel).\n79\t\n80\t## Vendored motion-primitives\n81\t\n82\tCopied in as owned source under `src/components/motion-primitives/`, not installed from npm.\n83\t\n84\t| Component | Used for | Notes |\n85\t|-----------|----------|-------|\n86\t| TextEffect or TextLoop | IX-01 | Role line only |\n87\t| MorphingDialog | IX-05 | Adoption is subject to the overlay accessibility ADR and its spike |\n88\t| AnimatedNumber with InView | IX-12 | Once |\n89\t| InfiniteSlider | IX-13 | not vendored (IX-13 dropped) |\n90\t| Tilt, Magnetic, Spotlight | IX-17 | Fine pointer only |\n91\t\n92\tNot vendored: Cursor, Dock and any other mouse-only primitive. Plan 01-05 completed it: principles, tokens, reduced-motion layers, ownership matrix, vendored primitives, the other 16 interaction specs and the element ownership check.\n\n## Ownership rule\n\n- Exactly one library animates any element: motion, react-spring, CSS or Lenis. Never two on the same element or property.\n- No Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates.\n- react-spring is scoped to IX-02, IX-03, IX-06 and IX-10 (velocity-carrying, tactile physics). Everything else uses motion, CSS or Lenis as the catalog says.\n\n## Principles\n\n- Motion never gates content. Name, role and CTAs are visible at first paint. The hero text effect runs only on the role line and never delays it.\n- Animate transform and opacity only, plus motion layout animations where an interaction needs them (IX-05, IX-07, IX-08, IX-11, IX-14).\n- Fine-pointer effects are gated by the media query `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and carry no hover-only content (MOT-04). Touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing.\n- `touch-action` is set only on small draggables. The project rail uses native horizontal scrolling, so vertical page scroll is never captured.\n- Infinite or looping motion pauses when off-screen or when the tab is hidden.\n- Motion budget: entrance animations take at most 420 ms; stagger is at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items; nothing blocks input.\n\n## Motion tokens\n\nCanonical home is `src/anim/tokens.ts`, with CSS mirrors `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`. One table drives both libraries so they feel like one system.\n\n| Token | Kind | motion format (stiffness, damping, mass) | react-spring format (tension, friction, mass) | Value |\n|-------|------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|\n| snappy | spring | 500, 32, 1 | 500, 32, 1 | presses, toggles |\n| gentle | spring | 170, 26, 1 | 170, 26, 1 | rail lift, layout settling |\n| bouncy | spring | 300, 14, 1 | 300, 14, 1 | playful overshoot, used sparingly |\n| fast | duration | n/a | n/a | 120 ms |\n| base | duration | n/a | n/a | 220 ms |\n| slow | duration | n/a | n/a | 420 ms |\n| ease-out | easing | n/a | n/a | cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) |\n\nreact-spring `tension` equals motion `stiffness` and `friction` equals `damping`. The spring numbers are starting values, to be tuned on a real iPhone and a real Android phone during the signature-rail work (Phase 4).\n\n## Reduced motion\n\nOne preference source (MOT-01): `useMotionPreference` reads `prefers-reduced-motion` with a `change` listener (users toggle it live) and feeds three consumers:\n\n- motion: `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (from `motion/react`).\n- react-spring: `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` from `@react-spring/web`, set in an effect with a dependency array and a cleanup that resets it.\n- CSS: the guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which also gates smooth scroll behind `no-preference`.\n\nLenis is not started under reduced motion (MOT-05). Motion's `user` mode still animates opacity, so text effects and other opacity-driven wrappers branch manually on the hook's `reduced` value.\n\n| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |\n|-------|-----------|--------|\n| L0 Progressive enhancement | Content is visible by default in HTML and CSS. Reveal wrappers set the hidden initial state only after mount on the client, and `<noscript>` guarantees visibility. | JS failure, slow hydration, crawlers, screenshots |\n| L1 CSS guard | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapses animation and transition durations to near zero, runs animations once and sets `scroll-behavior: auto`. | CSS transitions, keyframes, anchor scroll |\n| L2 motion | `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (\"user\", or \"always\" and \"never\" from an override). Disables transform and layout animations, keeps opacity and color. | All motion components, including vendored primitives |\n| L3 react-spring | `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` in the provider effect. Springs jump to their target. | All spring physics |\n| L4 Wrapper branches | Wrappers branch on `reduced` to drop parallax and scroll-linked transforms, stop loops and autoplay (text loop, infinite slider), disable fling, and swap transforms for short fades or nothing. | What L2 and L3 do not cover |\n| L5 Non-motion feedback | Pressed, focus and selected states read without motion, through color, outline or shape. | Reduced-motion users still get feedback |\n| L6 Visible toggle | Optional \"Reduce motion\" control persisted to localStorage and fed into `useMotionPreference`. Open decision, not committed. | Users whose OS setting is off but who want calm |\n\n## Ownership matrix\n\nMOT-02. Every interaction class has exactly one owner.\n\n| Interaction class | Owner | Why |\n|-------------------|-------|-----|\n| Mount, unmount and presence | motion (`AnimatePresence`) | Mature exit handling under React 19 |\n| Layout and shared-element morphs | motion (`layout`, `layoutId`) | react-spring has no equivalent |\n| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion (`useScroll`, `whileInView`) | Already bundled |\n| Text and number effects, motion-primitives prefabs | motion | The primitives are written against it |\n| Velocity physics, press-squish, rail lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring (`useSpring`, `useSprings`) | Continuous retargeting gives the tactile signature |\n| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail | CSS | Zero JS cost |\n| Desktop wheel smoothing | Lenis | Wheel only, off on touch |\n\nConstraints:\n\n- Install `@react-spring/web` at `~10.1.x` only; never the umbrella `react-spring` package.\n- Avoid `useTransition` in core UI; presence is motion's job, which keeps the react-spring v11 migration trivial.\n- `@use-gesture/react` is not added up front.\n- Import motion only from `motion/react`, never raw `framer-motion`.\n- Whether react-spring stays at all is decided after the rail is measured (bundle cost and feel).\n\n## Vendored motion-primitives\n\nCopied in as owned source under `src/components/motion-primitives/`, not installed from npm.\n\n| Component | Used for | Notes |\n|-----------|----------|-------|\n| TextEffect or TextLoop | IX-01 | Role line only |\n| MorphingDialog | IX-05 | Adoption is subject to the overlay accessibility ADR and its spike |\n| AnimatedNumber with InView | IX-12 | Once |\n| InfiniteSlider | IX-13 | not vendored (IX-13 dropped) |\n| Tilt, Magnetic, Spotlight | IX-17 | Fine pointer only |\n\nNot vendored: Cursor, Dock and any other mouse-only primitive. Each vendored file is patched for type-only imports and gets a reduced-motion branch.\n\n## Interaction catalog index\n\nIX-01 to IX-17 are fixed. IX-18 was added by the Phase 3 art direction. Properties, Token, Touch equivalent, Keyboard path, Reduced-motion fallback, Requirement, Build phase.\n\n### IX-01 Hero role-line text effect\n\n- Section: {#hero}\n- Trigger: on mount, once the role line is in view\n- Element: the role line only; the name, the CTAs and the rest of the hero are never animated by this effect\n- Owner library: motion\n- API: motion-primitives TextEffect or spring snappy\n- Touch equivalent: pointerdown and pointerup are the touch events, so a tap squishes the same way\n- Keyboard path: native buttons; Enter and Space keydown and keyup drive the same path\n- Keyboard path: IX-06 triggers the same lift from :focus-visible\n- Reduced-motion fallback: no lift or shift; the hovered item gets an elevation and outline change instead (L5)\n- Requirement: native scroll position only\n- Token: none, native scroll physics\n- Touch equivalent: this is the touch path; vertical page scroll stays untouched because no touch-action is set on the rail\n- Keyboard path: the container and items are focusable; arrow keys move between items (see IX-06) and the browser scrolls the focused item into view\n- Reduced-motion fallback: unchanged because the A Vite build cannot be served that way: the new site needs the \"GitHub Actions\" source, which changes how the live URL is published.\n17\t\n18\tThis development repository is not yet on GitHub. First the iPod site is tagged (`v1-ipod`) and that tag and a matching branch are pushed, so the old site stays recoverable. Only the source the site needs, the workflow and `docs/` are.\n27\t\n28\tThe step-by-step procedure, the workflow settings and the smoke test are in the [deploy runbook](../deploy-runbook.md).\n29\t\n30\t## Consequences\n31\t\n32\t- The live site and its history stay recoverable at every point: the old site is a tag, the cutover is one revertible commit, and nothing is rewritten.\n33\t- There may be a short window, while the Pages source is switched, in which the live URL returns a 404. This is possible but unverified (open decision OD-05); the switch and the workflow trigger are done back to back to keep it short.\n34\t- Staging on the project URL proves the Actions pipeline, base-path handling and asset paths before the user-site URL is touched.\n35\t- Staging requires pushing this repository to GitHub, which OD-01 no longer blocks.\n36\t\n37\t## Rollback\n38\t\n39\tIf the new site is broken or the switch goes wrong:\n40\t\n41\t1. Never force-push.\n44\t\n45\t## Alternatives considered\n46\t\n47\t- Replace the repository history with the new site (force-push). Rejected: it destroys the old site's history and the rollback path.\n48\t- Deploy the new site from a built-output branch instead of Actions. Rejected: it keeps build artifacts in git history and loses the CI gates.\n49\t- Keep the iPod site where it is and serve the new site only from the project URL. As a modal dialog it must:\n\n1. Trap keyboard focus inside the overlay while it is open.\n2. Close on Escape.\n3. Lock background scroll.\n4. Make the background inert, so assistive technology and tab order cannot reach it.\n5. Return focus to the rail item that opened it.\n6. Expose `role=\"dialog\"` with `aria-modal=\"true\"` and a label taken from the project title.\n7. Keep previous, next and close reachable and usable by keyboard.\n\nThe vendored `MorphingDialog` component from motion-primitives gives the morph animation. Its behavior on the seven points above has not been verified.\n\nThe motion spec splits responsibility the same way: motion animates the overlay, and the dialog primitive owns focus, Escape, inert background and scroll lock.\n\n## Decision\n\nMotion owns the overlay animation: `AnimatePresence` plus a shared `layoutId` morph from the rail item's inner card to the overlay panel, with a crossfade for previous and next. The dialog primitive owns everything on the checklist above: focus trap, Escape, inert background, scroll lock and focus return. The two concerns stay separate.\n\nA code spike checks `MorphingDialog` against the seven-point checklist before the rail ships. The spike itself is deferred to the interaction build (Phase 2 or 4) and is not run as part of the documentation work.\n\n- If every point passes, `MorphingDialog` is used as vendored.\n- If any point fails, the overlay uses a native `dialog` element opened with `showModal()`. Top-layer rendering makes the rest of the page inert and the `cancel` event handles Escape. Focus return and scroll lock are handled explicitly in our code. Motion animates only the inner panel; the `layoutId` morph targets that inner panel rendered inside the `dialog` element, not the `dialog` element itself.\n- Radix Dialog is considered only if both of the above fail, because it adds a dependency.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Overlay animation and overlay accessibility are separate concerns, so either primitive works with the same motion spec and the same reduced-motion fallback (instant open and close, no morph).\n- The native fallback costs a little explicit code (focus return, scroll lock) and no new dependency.\n- With the native fallback, the backdrop blur and the morph are applied to elements inside the `dialog`, because the `dialog` element's own box is not what animates.\n- The rail cannot ship until the spike result is recorded.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Adopt `MorphingDialog` without checking it. Rejected: an unverified focus trap and Escape path is an accessibility failure on the site's main interaction.\n- Always use the native `dialog` element. Not chosen as the default only because `MorphingDialog` may already pass and would then be less code; it stays the fallback.\n- Radix Dialog. The earlier rule and the remote therefore already disagreed. No option removes what is already public without rewriting remote history, which is never done here.\n10\t\n11\tThe owner was offered three choices before the next push: keep the planning area tracked and public, stop tracking it from this push on, or stop tracking it and also drop it from the unpushed local commits.\n12\t\n13\t## Decision\n14\t\n15\tThis ADR reverses, for this development repository only, the ADR-0001 rule that the working documents stay in a private planning area. A machine lock file written by the planning tool has no documentation value and is git-ignored.\n16\t\n17\tEvery other ADR-0001 rule still holds and is restated here so that this ADR carries everything that still applies:\n18\t\n19\t- The architecture doc, the ADRs and the deploy runbook live in the top-level `docs/` folder and are written to be published with the site.\n20\t- The reference folder (the source resume and reference videos) never goes into any public repository, and it stays git-ignored in this repo so a broad `git add` cannot stage it.\n21\t- The site repo (`aa-phan.github.io`) receives only the built site at cutover, never the planning area or the reference folder.\n22\t- Every file under `docs/` is self-contained: it never links into a private area, never names a private planning path or decision label, and never contains the phone number.\n23\t- The phone number is never published anywhere. Before every push the history and tree guards in the deploy runbook must print nothing.\n24\t\n25\t## Consequences\n26\t\n27\t- Plans, summaries, state snapshots and the assistant instruction file are browsable by anyone, for this phase and every future phase. Nothing pushed can be unpublished.\n28\t- The planning workflow keeps committing its documents, and they are backed up on GitHub.\n29\t- Privacy now rests on the guards rather than on a private area: the phone-number history and tree searches run before each push and print only commit hashes or file names.\n30\t- ADR-0001 is superseded by this ADR. Its file is unchanged apart from its Status line.\n31\t\n32\t## Alternatives considered\n33\t\n34\t- Stop tracking the planning area from this push on.
