No option removes what is already public without rewriting remote history, which is never done here.\n\nThe owner was offered three choices before the next push: keep the planning area tracked and public, stop tracking it from this push on, or stop tracking it and also drop it from the unpushed local commits.\n\n## Decision\n\nThis ADR reverses, for this development repository only, the ADR-0001 rule that the working documents stay in a private planning area. The planning area and the assistant instruction file stay tracked and public here. The workflow configuration and the state snapshot kept by the planning tool are committed with them, in one dedicated commit before the push. A machine lock file written by the planning tool has no documentation value and is git-ignored.\n\nEvery other ADR-0001 rule still holds and is restated here so that this ADR carries everything that still applies:\n\n- The architecture doc, the ADRs and the deploy runbook live in the top-level `docs/` folder and are written to be published with the site.\n- The reference folder (the source resume and reference videos) never goes into any public repository, and it stays git-ignored in this repo so a broad `git add` cannot stage it.\n- The site repo (`aa-phan.github.io`) receives only the built site at cutover, never the planning area or the reference folder.\n- Every file under `docs/` is self-contained: it never links into a private area, never names a private planning path or decision label, and never contains the phone number.\n- The phone number is never published anywhere. Before every push the history and tree guards in the deploy runbook must print nothing.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Plans, summaries, state snapshots and the assistant instruction file are browsable by anyone, for this phase and every future phase. Nothing pushed can be unpublished.\n- The planning workflow keeps committing its documents, and they are backed up on GitHub.\n- Privacy now rests on the guards rather than on a private area: the phone-number history and tree searches run before each push and print only commit hashes or file names.\n- ADR-0001 is superseded by this ADR. Its file is unchanged apart from its Status line.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Stop tracking the planning area from this push on. Rejected by the owner: the Phase 2 planning commits would still be pushed as history, and the planning documents would lose their remote backup.\n- Stop tracking it and also drop it from the unpushed local commits. Rejected by the owner: it rewrites local commit hashes quoted in summaries and has the same loss of backup, for little privacy gain since copies already public stay public.\n\n## Revisit when\n\nThe development repository and the site repository merge, the owner wants the planning area private again (which would also need a decision about the already-public history), or the planning area gains content that must not be public.\n","numLines":40,"startLine":1,"totalLines":40}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01JcakBWwxcxF6RThLaD92ex","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

--(typed, satisfies)--> app/Page --props--> sections --props--> layout, ui\n126\tassets/*     --(imagetools, hashed imports)--> image fields in content\n127\t```\n128\t\n129\tRuntime, all client-side with no network use beyond same-origin assets:\n130\t\n131\t- Theme: an inline script in the document head reads localStorage, falls back to prefers-color-scheme, and sets the data-theme attribute on the html element before first paint. The theme provider in React only changes the attribute and storage on a user toggle.\n132\t- Motion preference: the OS reduced-motion setting (plus an optional site override) feeds one hook, useMotionPreference, which configures both animation libraries and the wrapper components. See Reduced motion.\n133\t- Scroll-spy: an IntersectionObserver over the section ids drives useActiveSection, which highlights the current section in the navigation.\n134\t- Pointer and touch input drive react-spring values written straight to the DOM, with no React re-render per frame.\n135\t- Project detail: a click or tap sets local state in the Projects section, which opens an overlay with focus handling.\n136\t\n137\tThere is no global state library. Three small contexts exist: theme, motion preference and, optionally, the active section. Everything else is props.\n138\t\n139\t## Content model\n140\t\n141\tAll types live in src/content/schema.ts:\n142\t\n143\t- Profile: name, tagline, bio paragraphs, optional quote, photo (ImageAsset), contacts.\n144\t- ContactLink: kind (email, github, linkedin or instagram), label, href, whether it is external.\n145\t- ExperienceEntry: id, role, org, optional org URL, optional logo, dates (DateRange), location, bullets, optional highlights and stack.\n146\t- Project: id, title, context kind (personal, employer, course or hackathon) with a label, dates, stack, bullets, relatedExperienceId, featured, optional links and image.\n147\t- EducationEntry: id, degree, school, location, dates, gpa, optional track.\n148\t- SkillGroup: id, label, items as a string array.\n149\t- DateRange: ISO start and end (or present) plus a display label in one normalized format.\n150\t- ImageAsset: src, alt, width, height, optional srcset.\n151\t\n152\tRules:\n153\t\n154\t- Content modules use satisfies against the schema so a missing field fails typecheck.\n155\t- Ordering lives in the data (array order or a priority field), never in components.\n156\t- Copy is taken verbatim from the reviewed content inventory; any edit is recorded there with before and after, not made silently in code.\n157\t- The featured flag decides what appears first on mobile, so \"key info in seconds\" is a data decision.\n158\t- Content tests check that ids are unique, related ids resolve, every image has alt text, every external link is https, and dates parse in descending order.\n159\t- A phone number is not a field anywhere in the model, and must never appear in site copy, metadata or the served resume.\n160\t\n161\t## Design tokens\n162\t\n163\t- Exactly five role tokens per theme: text, background, primary, secondary, accent. Light and dark are authored separately, not inverted.\n164\t- Derived tokens (surface, border, muted text, link, focus ring and so on) are computed from the five roles with color-mix(in oklch, ...). A palette swap therefore edits one block and every derived value follows.\n165\t- The theme is selected by the data-theme attribute on the html element.\n166\t- Tailwind v4 is configured CSS-first: a custom dark variant is bound to [data-theme=dark] with @custom-variant, and an @theme inline block maps utilities to the CSS variables. There is no tailwind.config.js.\n167\t- No raw hex values in components. Components use semantic utilities only; a CI check greps for stray hex.\n168\t- A contrast test recomputes every text, UI and focus pair in both themes against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI) and fails the build on any miss.\n169\t- Spring and duration values that JavaScript needs are mirrored in CSS variables, with src/anim/tokens.ts as the canonical source for springs.\n170\t\n171\t## Animation layer\n172\t\n173\tsrc/anim/index.ts is the only animation import path for the rest of the app. It exposes a handful of semantic components and hooks, not library primitives.\n174\t\n175\t| Interaction class | Owner |\n176\t|-------------------|-------|\n177\t| Mount and unmount, presence, exit animations | motion |\n178\t| Layout and shared-element transitions | motion |\n179\t| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion |\n180\t| Text and number effects, stagger, ready-made motion-primitives prefabs | motion |\n181\t| Velocity-carrying physics: press-squish, rail hover lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring |\n182\t| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail swipe | CSS |\n183\t| Desktop wheel smoothing only | Lenis |\n184\t\n185\tThe rule: one library animates any given element. Never both libraries on one element or one property, and no Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates. If a vendored primitive duplicates a physics wrapper, one implementation is chosen per interaction and the other stays unused.\n186\t\n187\tSpring and duration tokens are defined once in src/anim/tokens.ts, exported in both libraries' formats (motion's stiffness and damping, react-spring's tension and friction), so the two feel like one system. Fine-pointer effects such as tilt, magnetic pull and spotlight are gated by (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing. Every wrapper reads the motion preference, renders an instant equivalent when reduced, forwards className, and never hides content in its initial CSS state.\n188\t\n189\t## Reduced motion\n190\t\n191\tOne preference source, useMotionPreference, combines the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting with an optional site override and feeds three consumers:\n192\t\n193\t- motion: the provider renders MotionConfig with its reducedMotion setting. This disables transform and layout animation but not opacity or color, so wrappers handle parallax, scroll-linked and autoplay effects explicitly.\n194\t- react-spring: the provider calls Globals.assign({ skipAnimation }) so every spring jumps to its target; the effect cleans up on change.\n195\t- CSS: a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) guard in base.css shortens transitions and animations and keeps scroll behavior native.\n196\t\n197\tContent is visible by default and is never hidden until JavaScript runs, and no wrapper applies a hidden initial state in CSS. Pressed, focused and selected states must read without motion (color, outline, shape). Lenis is off under reduced motion. The provider listens for changes to the media query, so a live OS toggle takes effect without a reload in both directions. Turning reduced motion off mid-visit also loads the motion feature chunk, which reduced-motion visitors otherwise never download.\n198\t\n199\t## Assets\n200\t\n201\t- Images live in src/assets/images/ and are imported as modules (hashed, long-cached). vite-imagetools produces AVIF and WebP variants and srcset with intrinsic width and height to prevent layout shift. Below-the-fold images lazy-load; the hero image is high priority.\n202\t- Fonts are self-hosted through Fontsource (variable, latin subset, font-display swap), at most two families. No third-party font CDN.\n203\t- Brand icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, Instagram, email) and UI glyphs (close, chevrons, download) are inline SVG components under src/components/ui/icons/. No icon package is installed. See ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 in the ADR log.\n204\t- The resume PDF served from public/ is the owner's phone-number-free export of the resume. The phone-number gate reads its text layer, link annotations and metadata, and rejects a stand-in file.\n205\t- Only images that are actually used migrate from the previous site, with EXIF metadata stripped. Template leftovers are left behind.\n206\t\n207\t## Build and deploy\n208\t\n209\tGitHub Actions builds the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages. The Vite base comes from the VITE_BASE environment variable: the project URL path (for example /aa-phan-portfolio-v2/) while staging, and / after the cutover to the user-site URL. Assets are module-imported so no absolute asset paths exist; anything under public/ that JavaScript references goes through import.meta.env.BASE_URL. CI also builds with the project-path base so a broken sub-path is caught before launch. The build has a second HTML entry, 404.html, a static not-found page that GitHub Pages serves for unknown paths. Steps, settings, cutover and rollback are in the deploy runbook (deploy-runbook.md).\n210\t\n211\t## Quality gates\n212\t\n213\t| Gate | Command | Fails the build when Import rules)\n|-- .github/workflows/       ci.yml, deploy.yml\n`-- src/\n    |-- main.tsx\n    |-- app/                 App.tsx, Page.tsx, Providers.tsx\n    |-- sections/            one folder per section (Hero, About, Experience,\n    |                        Projects, Skills, Education, Contact)\n    |-- layout/              Container, Section, SiteHeader, PillNav,\n    | index.ts         assembles siteContent with satisfies\n    |-- hooks/               useActiveSection, useTheme\n    |-- lib/                 cn.ts, date formatting, a11y helpers\n    |-- styles/\n    |   |-- index.css        tailwind import, dark variant, theme mapping\n    |   |-- tokens.css       role tokens, derived tokens, light and dark blocks\n    |   `-- base.css         resets, focus ring, reduced-motion guard, fonts\n    `-- assets/images/       hashed by Vite\n```\n\nThe animation folder is named anim/ rather than motion/ so it is never confused with the motion package or its motion/react import path.\n\n## Data flow\n\nBuild time:\n\n```text\ncontent/*.ts --(typed, satisfies)--> app/Page --props--> sections --props--> layout, ui\nassets/*     --(imagetools, hashed imports)--> image fields in content\n```\n\nRuntime, all client-side with no network use beyond same-origin assets:\n\n- Theme: an inline script in the document head reads localStorage, falls back to prefers-color-scheme, and sets the data-theme attribute on the html element before first paint. The theme provider in React only changes the attribute and storage on a user toggle.\n- Motion preference: the OS reduced-motion setting (plus an optional site override) feeds one hook, useMotionPreference, which configures both animation libraries and the wrapper components. See Reduced motion.\n- Scroll-spy: an IntersectionObserver over the section ids drives useActiveSection, which highlights the current section in the navigation.\n- Pointer and touch input drive react-spring values written straight to the DOM, with no React re-render per frame.\n- Project detail: a click or tap sets local state in the Projects section, which opens an overlay with focus handling.\n\nThere is no global state library. Three small contexts exist: theme, motion preference and, optionally, the active section. Everything else is props.\n\n## Content model\n\nAll types live in src/content/schema.ts:\n\n- Profile: name, tagline, bio paragraphs, optional quote, photo (ImageAsset), contacts.\n- ContactLink: kind (email, github, linkedin or instagram), label, href, whether it is external.\n- ExperienceEntry: id, role, org, optional org URL, optional logo, dates (DateRange), location, bullets, optional highlights and stack.\n- Project: id, title, context kind (personal, employer, course or hackathon) with a label, dates, stack, bullets, relatedExperienceId, featured, optional links and image.\n- EducationEntry: id, degree, school, location, dates, gpa, optional track.\n- SkillGroup: id, label, items as a string array.\n- DateRange: ISO start and end (or present) plus a display label in one normalized format.\n- ImageAsset: src, alt, width, height, optional srcset.\n\nRules:\n\n- Content modules use satisfies against the schema so a missing field fails typecheck.\n- Ordering lives in the data (array order or a priority field), never in components.\n- Copy is taken verbatim from the reviewed content inventory; any edit is recorded there with before and after, not made silently in code.\n- The featured flag decides what appears first on mobile, so \"key info in seconds\" is a data decision.\n- Content tests check that ids are unique, related ids resolve, every image has alt text, every external link is https, and dates parse in descending order.\n- A phone number is not a field anywhere in the model, and must never appear in site copy, metadata or the served resume.\n\n## Design tokens\n\n- Exactly five role tokens per theme: text, background, primary, secondary, accent. Light and dark are authored separately, not inverted.\n- Derived tokens (surface, border, muted text, link, focus ring and so on) are computed from the five roles with color-mix(in oklch, ...). A palette swap therefore edits one block and every derived value follows.\n- The theme is selected by the data-theme attribute on the html element.\n- Tailwind v4 is configured CSS-first: a custom dark variant is bound to [data-theme=dark] with @custom-variant, and an @theme inline block maps utilities to the CSS variables. There is no tailwind.config.js.\n- No raw hex values in components. Components use semantic utilities only; a CI check greps for stray hex.\n- A contrast test recomputes every text, UI and focus pair in both themes against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI) and fails the build on any miss.\n- Spring and duration values that JavaScript needs are mirrored in CSS variables, with src/anim/tokens.ts as the canonical source for springs.\n\n## Animation layer\n\nsrc/anim/index.ts is the only animation import path for the rest of the app. It exposes a handful of semantic components and hooks, not library primitives.\n\n| Interaction class | Owner |\n|-------------------|-------|\n| Mount and unmount, presence, exit animations | motion |\n| Layout and shared-element transitions | motion |\n| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion |\n| Text and number effects, stagger, ready-made motion-primitives prefabs | motion |\n| Velocity-carrying physics: press-squish, rail hover lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring |\n| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail swipe | CSS |\n| Desktop wheel smoothing only | Lenis |\n\nThe rule: one library animates any given element. Never both libraries on one element or one property, and no Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates. If a vendored primitive duplicates a physics wrapper, one implementation is chosen per interaction and the other stays unused.\n\nSpring and duration tokens are defined once in src/anim/tokens.ts, exported in both libraries' formats (motion's stiffness and damping, react-spring's tension and friction), so the two feel like one system. Fine-pointer effects such as tilt, magnetic pull and spotlight are gated by (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing. Every wrapper reads the motion preference, renders an instant equivalent when reduced, forwards className, and never hides content in its initial CSS state.\n\n## Reduced motion\n\nOne preference source, useMotionPreference, combines the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting with an optional site override and feeds three consumers:\n\n- motion: the provider renders MotionConfig with its reducedMotion setting. This disables transform and layout animation but not opacity or color, so wrappers handle parallax, scroll-linked and autoplay effects explicitly.\n- react-spring: the provider calls Globals.assign({ skipAnimation }) so every spring jumps to its target; the effect cleans up on change.\n- CSS: a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) guard in base.css shortens transitions and animations and keeps scroll behavior native.\n\nContent is visible by default and is never hidden until JavaScript runs, and no wrapper applies a hidden initial state in CSS. Pressed, focused and selected states must read without motion (color, outline, shape). Lenis is off under reduced motion. The provider listens for changes to the media query, so a live OS toggle takes effect without a reload in both directions. Turning reduced motion off mid-visit also loads the motion feature chunk, which reduced-motion visitors otherwise never download.\n\n## Assets\n\n- Images live in src/assets/images/ and are imported as modules (hashed, long-cached). vite-imagetools produces AVIF and WebP variants and srcset with intrinsic width and height to prevent layout shift. Below-the-fold images lazy-load; the hero image is high priority.\n- Fonts are self-hosted through Fontsource (variable, latin subset, font-display swap), at most two families. No third-party font CDN.\n- Brand icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, Instagram, email) and UI glyphs (close, chevrons, download) are inline SVG components under src/components/ui/icons/. No icon package is installed. See ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 in the ADR log.\n- The resume PDF served from public/ is the owner's phone-number-free export of the resume. The phone-number gate reads its text layer, link annotations and metadata, and rejects a stand-in file.\n- Only images that are actually used migrate from the previous site, with EXIF metadata stripped. Template leftovers are left behind.\n\n## Build and deploy\n\nGitHub Actions builds the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages. The Vite base comes from the VITE_BASE environment variable: the project URL path (for example /aa-phan-portfolio-v2/) while staging, and / after the cutover to the user-site URL. Assets are module-imported so no absolute asset paths exist; anything under public/ that JavaScript references goes through import.meta.env.BASE_URL. CI also builds with the project-path base so a broken sub-path is caught before launch. The build has a second HTML entry, 404.html, a static not-found page that GitHub Pages serves for unknown paths. Steps, settings, cutover and rollback are in the deploy runbook (deploy-runbook.md).\n\n## Quality gates\n\n| Gate | Command | Fails the build when |\n|------|---------|----------------------|\n|
